data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The distinction between truly independent and merely uncorrelated failures is revealed by interventions on the postulated shared cause: truly independent failures will not systematically co-vary when a shared latent factor is perturbed, whereas synchronized failures will.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the shared cause is non-manipulable (e.g., a law of physics or a global macroeconomic event), the intervention cannot be performed.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the system is so opaque that the shared latent variable cannot be identified, the test cannot be applied.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If failures are merely uncorrelated but share a hidden common cause, manipulating that cause (e.g., artificially constraining a specific cloud provider's API) will force the independent failures to manifest as perfectly correlated. If the failures are truly independent, perturbing one node's environment will not predictably trigger failures in distant nodes. This follows a counterfactual logic: if we had changed the shared input, would the failures have been different?","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
